newsitem.title: INDIA: India cotton firms, exporters face limited arrivals.
newsitem.headline: India cotton firms, exporters face limited arrivals.

text.p: Cotton prices extended gains on the local market despite slow mill buying, as increased exporter demand faced limited arrivals.
Export enquiries focussed on medium and long staple cotton.

In the spot deals Bengal-deshi rose by 5 rupees at 915/960 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned moved up by 10 rupees at 1,575/1,670 rupees per maund. F-414 lifted by 5 rupees at 1,910/1,940 rupees per maund while Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) rose by the 200 rupees at 13,700/14,000 rupees per candy (355.56 kg). Long-staple Gujarat Sankar-4 (superior variety) climbed up from 18,500/19,700 rupees to 18,700/19,800 rupees per candy.
Arrivals remained low on account of ongoing nationwide strike by the transport operators as well as unseaonal rain in some producing centres.
Indian transporters are on strike from April 1 to protest against service tax and hike in the insurance premium.
The Bombay cotton market will remain closed on Tuesday for a Hindu festival and reopen on Wedesday.
